column4: Salih calls the she-camel God's sign and tells his people to leave her on God's earth. It repeats the distinctive living-sign scene with its own command to preserve what identifies the message.
God says that Jesus will be made a sign for people and a mercy. The promised child is therefore a living, publicly legible sign before the later world-sign formulations.
The abandoned houses of the wrongdoing people are called a sign for people who know. Their visible desolation is a trace that can be read, like the ruined town in 15:75.
God says He left from the destroyed town a clear sign for people who understand. This makes the remaining ruin itself an intelligible mark rather than merely a past event.
The verse says that the preceding vessel or event was left as a sign and asks who will remember. Its own contribution is the preservation of a trace for recognition across time.
God says He left Noah among later generations; the following greeting makes the lasting mention favorable. This supplies another Qur'anic form of the good name that survives among people.
God says He left Abraham among later generations; the next verse's greeting clarifies the enduring honorable remembrance, parallel to a lofty truthful mention.
God says He left Moses and Aaron among later generations. The line preserves their paired public remembrance after the rescue narrative.
God says He left Elijah among later generations; the following greeting completes the image of a prophet's name remaining recognizable after him.
The people of Aad build an ayah on every high place for play. A raised monument is called a sign, but its vain construction reverses the section's sign that leads to genuine recognition.
The worshippers are described by God's dye, صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ. This is a specific parallel to the branded mark: a bestowed imprint identifies those devoted to its giver.
On the Day when faces whiten and blacken, the blackened faces are addressed for disbelief. Visible color becomes a boundary-mark that makes contrary moral outcomes legible.

Mountains, rivers, and routes are placed so people may be guided; 16:16 follows by naming landmarks and guiding stars. This ayah supplies the terrain and paths through which the next ayah's markers work.
Monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques are places in which God's name is much mentioned. The name is thus preserved and raised publicly in built spaces of worship.
Those who reject the Hereafter give the angels female names. This is a concrete false naming that contrasts with a name grounded in what it truly makes known.
After the command to read in the Lord's name, God is described as teaching by the pen. Writing supplies a material practice through which names and distinguishing signs become knowable.
God teaches the human what he did not know. This completes the opening command to read in the Lord's name by making learning and recognition its stated divine gift.
